note: Maine U.S. Senate and governor races, researched Oct. 25, 2026.

candidates.name: Susan Collins
candidates.bio: U.S. senator since 1997 and chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee.

source.title: guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Collins introduced a bill with Sen. Murkowski to write the Roe v. Wade and Casey protections into law, but voted against the Women's Health Protection Act (Senate roll call 170, 2022), citing missing conscience protections
guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Collins called the overturning of Roe v. Wade a radical jolt to the country
guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Collins voted to extend the residential clean energy credit but against keeping the wind and solar tax credits (Senate roll calls 365 and 364, 2025)

guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Collins sponsored a ban on offshore drilling in the Gulf of Maine (S. 1472) and voted against opening the Arctic refuge's coastal plain to drilling (Senate roll call 632, 2025)

guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Collins voted to keep mining limits near the Boundary Waters (Senate roll call 84, 2026) but to undo limits on seven hazardous air pollutants (Senate roll call 229, 2025)
guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Collins voted for the infrastructure law (Senate roll call 314, 2021)
guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Collins calls for expanded access to workforce training
guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Collins voted to extend ACA premium subsidies (Maine Public, Dec. 2025)

guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Collins voted against the 2025 tax and spending law over its Medicaid cuts (Senate roll call 372) and proposed taxing the ultrawealthy to help rural hospitals (S.Amdt. 2812)
source.quote: harmful impact it will have on Medicaid

source.title: guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Collins voted for the 2017 tax cuts and against their 2025 extension, and proposed a tax increase on the ultrawealthy to fund rural hospitals (S.Amdt. 2812)

guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Collins voted for about $70 billion in new ICE and border funding twice in 2026, but also to move some ICE money to Medicaid (Senate roll call 18, 2026)
guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Collins voted in April 2026 to end the Iran hostilities at the War Powers Act's 60-day mark, after voting against a March limit (Senate roll call 46)
source.quote: Further military action against Iran must have a clear mission.

source.title: guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Collins first voted against limiting the Iran war, then voted to end the hostilities at the 60-day mark
guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Collins sponsored the Protect America's Workforce Act (S. 2837) to restore union rights at federal agencies
guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Collins introduced the Respect for Marriage Act (S. 4556, 2022)
guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Collins voted for a federal ban on transgender athletes in girls' and women's sports (S. 9; Senate roll call 100, 2025)
guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Collins introduced a bill to raise the federal minimum wage to $11 by 2028, indexed to inflation (S. 2785, 2023)
guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Collins supports voter ID (Press Herald, Feb. 2026); she voted for proof of citizenship at registration, then later against it
source.quote: an ID at the polls…will improve the security of our federal elections

candidates.name: Troy Jackson
candidates.bio: Former president of the Maine Senate (2018 to 2024) and a logger from Allagash.

source.title: guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Jackson would pass a federal right to abortion
guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Jackson sponsored LD 1619 (2023), allowing abortion after 24 weeks when a doctor deems it necessary, and voted against a 2017 fetal-protection bill
guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Jackson on climate
source.quote: Climate change is a profound threat to our environment and economy.

source.title: guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Jackson voted to boost offshore wind energy in Maine and promoted wood-based energy
guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Jackson sponsored a 2021 bill to ban synthetic herbicide spraying in forestry (SP 58) and pledges to protect air and water from chemicals like PFAS
guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Jackson sponsored a bill creating a drug treatment court in Aroostook County
guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Jackson's housing plan would stop Wall Street from buying up Maine
guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Jackson would offer housing tax credits and down-payment help
guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Jackson would invest in child care
guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Jackson supports Medicare for All
guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Jackson supports Medicare for All nationally and a public option in Maine (Maine Public, April 2026)
guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Jackson supports Medicare for All
source.quote: Healthcare is not, in my mind, a for-profit industry.

source.title: guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Jackson voted to cap prescription drug costs at a reference rate (SP 745)
guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Jackson would abolish ICE and opposes its $70 billion funding increase
guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Jackson says people here illegally or who commit crimes should be deported through a better process (Washington Post opinion, July 2026)
guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Jackson calls the Iran war foolish and illegal
guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Jackson would put diplomacy ahead of open-ended military action (Bangor Daily News, Aug. 2026)
guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Jackson would demand real congressional oversight of the Iran war
guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Jackson voted to expand public-sector collective bargaining (2019) and against a right-to-work bill
source.quote: give every worker the freedom to organize a union

source.title: guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Jackson would pass comprehensive civil rights protections for LGBTQ+ people
guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Jackson calls his 2009 vote against same-sex marriage his worst vote ever
guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Jackson opposes banning transgender athletes from women's sports
guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Jackson voted to raise Maine's minimum wage to $15 with cost-of-living increases (2023)
guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Jackson on taxes
source.quote: tax the billionaires and make sure greedy corporations pay their fair share

source.title: guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Jackson voted to add an income tax bracket above $500,000 while expanding the lowest bracket
source.quote: I don't believe in income tax cuts for wealthy people.

source.title: guides.vote, 2026 Maine U.S. Senate voters guide: Jackson opposed 2025's Question 1, which would have cut absentee voting days and limited drop boxes

candidates.name: Hannah Pingree
candidates.bio: Speaker of the Maine House from 2008 to 2010, later director of Gov. Janet Mills's policy office and co-chair of the Maine Climate Council.

source.title: Maine Public candidate questionnaire, April 17, 2026: Pingree supports the right to an abortion and says she defended reproductive rights as speaker
Maine Public candidate questionnaire, April 17, 2026: Pingree says she stood up for marriage equality as speaker in 2009
Maine Public candidate questionnaire, April 17, 2026: Pingree opposes banning transgender athletes from girls' and women's sports and weakening the Maine Human Rights Act
Maine Public candidate questionnaire, April 17, 2026: Pingree says photo ID should not be required to vote and would veto any bill that undermines voting rights
Maine Public candidate questionnaire, April 17, 2026: Pingree would make Maine's free community college permanent
Maine Public candidate questionnaire, April 17, 2026: Pingree would expand apprenticeships
Maine Public candidate questionnaire, April 17, 2026: Pingree would invest $100 million a year in building and preserving housing
Maine Public candidate questionnaire, April 17, 2026: Pingree would crack down on out-of-state corporations and private equity displacing Maine families from homes
Maine Public candidate questionnaire, April 17, 2026: Pingree would cut red tape and streamline housing permits
Maine Public candidate questionnaire, April 17, 2026: Pingree would work to reduce evictions
Maine Public candidate questionnaire, April 17, 2026: Pingree would raise the homestead exemption and widen the Property Tax Fairness Credit
Maine Public candidate questionnaire, April 17, 2026: Pingree says health care is a right
Maine Public candidate questionnaire, April 17, 2026: Pingree would create a state-backed public insurance option and streamline MaineCare enrollment
Maine Public candidate questionnaire, April 17, 2026: Pingree would add mental health to primary care, deploy mobile crisis teams and expand addiction recovery
Maine Public candidate questionnaire, April 17, 2026: Pingree would use the federal rural health grant to prevent rural closures and recruit providers
Maine Public candidate questionnaire, April 17, 2026: Pingree advanced Maine's first greenhouse gas targets and its entry into the regional carbon market (RGGI)
Maine Public candidate questionnaire, April 17, 2026: Pingree would expand affordable clean energy and clean energy jobs
Maine Public candidate questionnaire, April 17, 2026: Pingree passed the Kid-Safe Products Act on toxic chemicals and would hold corporate polluters accountable
Maine Public candidate questionnaire, April 17, 2026: Pingree agrees an immigrant workforce is essential to Maine's economy
Maine Public debate report, Oct. 9, 2026: Pingree criticizes Charles for wanting an immigration detention center in Maine
source.quote: open an Alligator Alcatraz to detain people here

source.title: Maine Public candidate questionnaire, April 17, 2026: Pingree supports free speech and press, including speech she considers biased

candidates.name: Bobby Charles
candidates.bio: Former assistant U.S. secretary of state for counter-narcotics and a Navy veteran.

source.title: Maine Public debate report, Oct. 9, 2026: Charles blames Maine's new law limiting police cooperation with ICE and wants agencies to cooperate
source.quote: State and local and federal law enforcement should always be talking to each other.

source.title: Maine Public debate report, Oct. 9, 2026: Charles disagrees with the tariffs on Canada
Maine Public debate report, Oct. 9, 2026: Charles opposes rolling back power plant emission standards
Bobby Charles campaign site: Charles would cut taxes on businesses and working families and suspend the gas tax

candidates.name: Rick Bennett
candidates.bio: Maine state senator from Oxford and Senate president from 2001 to 2002, running as an independent after leaving the Republican Party.

source.title: Maine Public candidate questionnaire, Sept. 22, 2026: Bennett supports the right to an abortion and includes reproductive care in the health care he calls a right
Maine Public candidate questionnaire, Sept. 22, 2026: Bennett opposes banning transgender athletes from girls' and women's sports and weakening the Maine Human Rights Act
Maine Public candidate questionnaire, Sept. 22, 2026: Bennett says photo ID should be required to vote
Maine Public candidate questionnaire, Sept. 22, 2026: Bennett supports tuition-free community college
Maine Public candidate questionnaire, Sept. 22, 2026: Bennett would expand workforce training and apprenticeships
Maine Public candidate questionnaire, Sept. 22, 2026: Bennett would reduce down payments for first-time homebuyers and offer direct mortgage assistance
Maine Public candidate questionnaire, Sept. 22, 2026: Bennett would clear permitting and infrastructure bottlenecks for new housing
Maine Public candidate questionnaire, Sept. 22, 2026: Bennett would apply the Property Tax Fairness Credit directly to tax bills and expand relief for older Mainers
Maine Public candidate questionnaire, Sept. 22, 2026: Bennett says health care is a right and would move Maine toward universal coverage
Maine Public debate report, Oct. 9, 2026: Bennett would keep the Medicaid expansion voters approved in 2017
Maine Public candidate questionnaire, Sept. 22, 2026: Bennett would strengthen behavioral health care
Maine Public candidate questionnaire, Sept. 22, 2026: Bennett would expand heat pumps, storage and grid upgrades and create a Maine Generation Authority for in-state renewable power
Maine Public candidate questionnaire, Sept. 22, 2026: Bennett says clean energy policy must cut emissions while lowering costs
Maine Public debate report, Oct. 9, 2026: Bennett supports Maine's law limiting cooperation with ICE
source.quote: ICE has not earned the benefit of the doubt.

source.title: Maine Public candidate questionnaire, Sept. 22, 2026: Bennett agrees an immigrant workforce is essential to Maine's economy
Maine Public candidate questionnaire, Sept. 22, 2026: Bennett supports free speech and press, including speech he considers biased
